The $r$th term of an arithmetic series is $(2r-5)$.
(a)  Write down the first three terms of this series.
(2)
(b)  State the value of the common difference.
(1)
(c)  Show that $\sum_{r=1}^{n}(2r-5) = n(n-4)$.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $-3,\ -1,\ 1$   B1: One correct   B1 B1   (2)
(b) $2$   (ft only if terms in (a) are in arithmetic progression)   B1ft   (1)
(c) Sum $= \frac{1}{2}n\{2(-3)+(n-1)(2)\}$  or  $\frac{1}{2}n\{(-3)+(2n-5)\}$   M1 A1ft
$=\frac{1}{2}n\{2n-8\}=n(n-4)$   (Not just $n^2-4n$)   (*)   A1   (3)

questions.stem:
The gradient of the curve $C$ is given by
$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = (3x-1)^2$.

The point $P(1, 4)$ lies on $C$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a)  Find an equation of the normal to $C$ at $P$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Evaluate gradient at $x=1$ to get 4,  Grad. of normal $=-\frac{1}{m}$ $\left(=-\frac{1}{4}\right)$   B1, M1
Equation of normal: $y-4=-\frac{1}{4}(x-1)$  ($4y=-x+17$)   M1 A1   (4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b)  Find an equation for the curve $C$ in the form $y = \mathrm{f}(x)$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $(3x-1)^2=9x^2-6x+1$   (May be seen elsewhere)   B1
Integrate: $\frac{9x^3}{3}-\frac{6x^2}{2}+x$  $(+C)$   M1 A1ft
Substitute $(1,4)$ to find $c=\ldots$,   $c=3$   ($y=3x^3-3x^2+x+3$)   M1, A1cso   (5)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c)  Using $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = (3x-1)^2$, show that there is no point on $C$ at which the tangent is parallel to the line $y = 1-2x$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) Gradient of given line is $-2$   B1
Gradient of (tangent to) $C$ is $\geqslant 0$ (allow $>0$), so can never equal $-2$.   B1   (2)
11
